revisions.note: Digital-assets research note (institutional-client only), via The Block’s coverage.
“Half-Year 2026” reframes the scenarios ($203B–$1.6T): the May base becomes the bull case. A {stat:drift_x}× cut, {stat:drift_weeks_words} weeks apart.
“Chainlink: Owning the rails” – lands within {stat:fork_gap_pct}% of 21Shares’ $350B by a completely different definitional route.
Binance Half-Year 2026 and SC “Owning the rails” folded into the chart, tables and matrix.
Grayscale’s ~$30B “today” figure and permissioned-rails lean added; every figure on this page now downloadable as data.json / data.csv / positions.csv.

Standard Chartered’s $4T is now labelled as the 2028 figure it is (it sat on the 2030 chart unmarked); desk and forecast counts, the “same month” claim, the permissioned-layer multiple (was ten-fold, now ~{stat:permissioned_x}×) and the Binance cut interval ({stat:drift_weeks_words} weeks, was ten) corrected. Dataset restructured: one record per figure with horizon, as-of date and unit; stable desk ids; defined position vocabularies; JSON Schema and data dictionary.

chart_forecast.title: Market-size forecasts · 2030 horizon (SC: 2028)
chart_forecast.note_log: Log scale – marks are **dots, not bars**: on a log axis there is no zero, so length means nothing. Read position only.
chart_forecast.note_linear: Linear scale – the smallest forecast nearly vanishes. *That* {stat:fc_spread}× gap is the disagreement.

chart_today.title: Market size – today
chart_today.note_log: Log scale – dots, not bars. {stat:td_desks_Words} desks, {stat:td_numbers_words} numbers, same market.
chart_today.note_linear: Linear scale – definitional choices swing today’s number ~{stat:td_spread}×. Colour is the definition.

chart_byscope.title: 2030 forecasts · grouped by scope
chart_byscope.note: Group the {stat:fc_n_words} forecasts by what they count and the {stat:fc_spread}× spread collapses: within a scope bucket the desks land ≤{stat:scope_max_spread}× apart. Same market – the disagreement is the definition, not the conviction.
